items.stem: In Elixir, what does the expression {:ok, value} = {:ok, 42} do?

options.text: It pattern-matches, binding value to 42 because both sides share the {:ok, _} shape
options.rationale: Correct: = is the match operator; the shapes agree so value is bound to 42.

options.text: It compares the two tuples and returns a boolean
options.rationale: = matches and binds; it does not return a boolean comparison.

options.text: It mutates the tuple on the right
options.rationale: Elixir data is immutable; nothing is mutated.

options.text: It raises because :ok is not a variable
options.rationale: :ok is a literal atom that matches the literal on the right, so no error is raised.

items.explanation: Correct: = is the match operator; the shapes agree so value is bound to 42.

items.stem: Which statements about processes on the BEAM are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: Processes are lightweight and isolated, communicating only by message passing
options.rationale: Correct: BEAM processes share no memory and coordinate through messages.

options.text: A crash in one process does not corrupt another's memory
options.rationale: Correct: isolation means one process crashing cannot corrupt another; supervisors handle restart.

options.text: Processes share mutable global memory for speed
options.rationale: BEAM processes share nothing; there is no shared mutable memory.

options.text: Each process maps one-to-one to an OS thread
options.rationale: The scheduler multiplexes many lightweight processes onto a few OS threads.

items.explanation: Correct: BEAM processes share no memory and coordinate through messages.; Correct: isolation means one process crashing cannot corrupt another; supervisors handle restart.

items.stem: What is the role of a supervisor in OTP?

options.text: To monitor child processes and restart them according to a strategy when they crash
options.rationale: Correct: supervisors apply a restart strategy to keep the system healthy under the let-it-crash model.

options.text: To prevent any child process from ever crashing
options.rationale: Supervisors do not prevent crashes; they react to them.

options.text: To store the application's user data
options.rationale: Supervisors manage lifecycles, not data storage.
Supervision is a runtime concern, unrelated to compilation.

items.explanation: Correct: supervisors apply a restart strategy to keep the system healthy under the let-it-crash model.
